neighbours.label: the article or connective just before a reversal word (quite the opposite, exactly the reverse, und umgekehrt), predicting 'opposite/contrary', versus 'the' in ordinary phrases
fire: Critics said the plan would fail, but quite the opposite turned out to be true.
Most people assume older drivers are slower. Exactly the opposite is the case.
He did not seem angry at all; just the opposite, he laughed about it.
They thought the medicine would calm him, but it did quite the reverse.
I expected the town to be empty, but quite the opposite: it was packed.
Teachers feared the phones would distract pupils, yet exactly the reverse happened.
She was not shy about it; quite the contrary, she told everyone.
Many believe cold weather causes colds, but the research shows just the opposite.
quiet: Critics said the plan would work, and the results turned out to be good.
Most people assume older drivers are slower. Exactly the same holds for cyclists.
He came home late and laughed about the long wait at the station.
They thought the medicine would help him, and it did within a day.
I expected the town to be busy, and it was packed with tourists.
Teachers bought new phones for the office, and the school paid for them.
She walked to the store and told everyone about the sale.
Many people enjoy cold weather, and the research shows it helps sleep.
